text:
sam: Quick sync — we need to decide sidecar vs proxy for propagating billing attributes across services. thinking about latency, failure modes, and migration path. opinion?
jessie: my bias is sidecar for correctness. keeps logic local, easier to view/debug per-service. but more work for SDKs and host images.
lee: proxy wins for ops consistency — one place to enforce header canonicalization and worst-case fallback. also simpler for non-JS runtimes.
tia: tradeoffs: sidecar increases per-host resource footprint, but lets us avoid touching app code. proxy centralizes TLS/mtu constraints and can add batching for lookups.
sam: good points. latency: proxy adds an extra network hop on every request; sidecar adds local processing but no extra hop. which is better for our 50ms p95 SLO?
jessie: sidecar should be <1ms for header handling. proxy hop could be ~5-10ms depending on topology. at 50ms p95 that matters for chat endpoints.
lee: remember we can co-locate proxy on the node for minimal hop, but still need env-specific routing. not trivial for k8s + VM mix.
tia: failure semantics: with sidecar, app can degrade gracefully by reading cached attributes or falling back to default tenant. proxy failure is easier to detect/metrics but may create wider blast radius.
obs-bot: incident: last week we saw a proxy outage affect 30% of requests for 3m; sidecars would have isolated impact to nodes. :spiral_note_pad:
sam: deployment complexity: sidecar requires packaging for each runtime, plus CI image updates. proxy is single binary/service we manage.
jessie: also think about sampling & late enrichment. if we enrich at the proxy, we might drop data before the app sees it, which complicates debug when sampling decisions use enriched attrs.
lee: good call. If sampling uses billing attrs we must ensure enrichment happens before sampling. That suggests sidecar or pre-app proxy.
tia: migration idea: start with proxy path that is non-authoritative (adds attributes but leaves header if app sets it). then roll a sidecar as optional that can be toggled to authoritative per-service.
sam: can we standardize a header format that both proxy and sidecar speak? e.g. X-RW-Attr: base64(json) and signature X-RW-Sig. tooling can validate sigs.
jessie: yes please. include versioning: v1; later we can compress. also add a small footprint canonicalizer: map keys to short codes to reduce header size.
lee: what about signing? HMAC per-cluster key via KMS. proxy can sign when authoritative; sidecar can verify. rotation plan needed.
tia: ops: need metrics on attr-missing, verification-fail, propagation-latency. if we roll proxy first, add a canary that only handles traffic for low-volume services.
sam: rollout plan sketch: 1) define header spec and sig scheme; 2) implement proxy non-authoritative that injects attrs for services that opt-in; 3) add observability (metrics + traces) for propagation; 4) implement sidecar for critical low-latency services and flip to authoritative there; 5) deprecate proxy-authoritative mode after coverage.
jessie: QA: create a harness that replays traces and validates that attr values are identical across both paths. also include fuzz tests for malformed headers and signature errors.
lee: config hell: how do we decide per-service canonical source? propose a service annotation in service registry: attr_source = [app, sidecar, proxy]. default proxy for legacy, sidecar for new.
tia: and a safety net: if verification fails, do NOT drop attrs — mark as invalid and route to fallback billing pipeline for manual reconciliation.
obs-bot: note: sampling policies touched. add a flag to sampling controller to accept external attr overrides only from verified headers.
sam: open tasks: 1) draft header spec doc, 2) prototype proxy non-authoritative, 3) perf benchmark for sidecar path under 1k rps, 4) map of services by latency sensitivity. volunteers?
jessie: I'll draft the header & signature spec. 2-day spike.
lee: I'll prototype proxy non-auth canary and set up metrics. need a small k8s job to route test traffic.
tia: I'll run perf benchmarks for sidecar in nodejs + python SDKs and list packaging requirements.
sam: awesome. I'll create the rollout checklist and update the service registry annotation PR. we'll reconvene Thurs 9am. :thumbsup:
jessie: added a few notes in the draft doc about max header size and fallback chunking strategy.
lee: FYI I found an existing npm sidecar-helper we'll reuse for node services.
tia: putting perf numbers in #perf once done.
sam: thanks all — keep thread alive for any gotchas.
